title: Philidor Defense: Légal's mate
line: White gives up the queen and mates with three minor pieces, if Black takes it.

steps.text: The Philidor Defense. Here Black pins White's knight to the queen, often seen at club level; masters prefer the bishop to e7.
Both sides bring a knight out. Then White's pinned knight takes on e5 and leaves its queen to be taken.
If you take the queen, the bishop checks on f7 and the other knight mates: Légal's mate, three minor pieces against the king.
Back before the queen grab. Take the knight on e5 instead: the pin was a bluff, and now White loses a piece.

wrong.g4d1: That is the mate you just saw: the bishop checks on f7 and the knight mates.
wrong.d6e5: The queen takes your bishop on g4, and White is a pawn up.

steps.hint: Take the piece that just landed on e5.
steps.after: If the queen takes your bishop, your knight takes the queen. So White steps the bishop back.

steps.text: Trade bishops. You keep the extra knight, and the white queen can no longer take your bishop.
steps.after: You are a piece up. A queen offer is not always a gift: look at what follows before you take.

summary: A queen left to be taken can be bait for mate. Before you take it, look at what the other pieces do to your king.
